slides.title: Physics to Arrays and Plots
slides.subtitle: Week 1 | From Motion to MATLAB
slides.claim: One familiar model becomes arrays, a plot, and validation.
slides.notes: Opening source block and visual provenance required.

slides.title: Arrays store physical moments
slides.subtitle: Each index identifies one measurement time
slides.claim: An array index selects a physically meaningful time.
visibleCopy: The number in parentheses selects one physical moment from the array
slides.notes: Eleven samples map explicitly to indices 1–11.

slides.title: A labelled plot turns values into evidence
slides.subtitle: Axes, units, and shape must agree with the model
slides.claim: A plot tests a stated physical prediction.
visibleCopy: Does the curve match all three predictions?

slides.title: A boundary check can reveal an error that a smooth curve hides
slides.subtitle: Use a known condition before trusting the full result
slides.claim: The initial condition is an executable physical check.
visibleCopy: The first array value satisfies the launch condition
A smooth graph is not enough: test at least one value that physics already tells you

slides.title: Names and units keep the model readable
slides.subtitle: Translate each physical quantity before writing code
slides.claim: Meaningful MATLAB names preserve physical units.
visibleCopy: Readable names reduce syntax mistakes and make unit checks easier
slides.notes: Uses y_m, t_s, v0_mps, and g_mps2 conventions. Gravitational acceleration uses the evaluation-gold/pale-gold semantic; symbol-g.tex/SVG/PNG was regenerated with foreground #C98A16, not purple.

slides.title: Short code should expose the physics
slides.subtitle: The algorithm appears before the MATLAB syntax
slides.claim: A plain-language algorithm precedes the short MATLAB fragment.
visibleCopy:
% model parameters
v0 = 20;       % m/s
g  = 9.81;     % m/s^2

% array of times
t = linspace(0,4,11);

% height at every time
y = v0.*t - 0.5*g.*t.^2;

plot(t,y,'LineWidth',2)
y(1)            % boundary check
.* and .^ apply the operation to every array element
slides.notes: Core code is intentionally short and traceable.

slides.title: The equation links each term to motion
slides.subtitle: Read the model from left to right before evaluating it
slides.claim: Every term maps to a physical contribution and has metres as its unit.
visibleCopy: Unit check: every term on the right must have units of metres

slides.title: Build the time array first
slides.subtitle: The model needs one time value for each computed height
slides.claim: Colon notation and linspace can create the same 41-sample time array.

slides.title: Dots tell MATLAB to work through an array
slides.subtitle: Use element-wise operators when time contains many values
slides.claim: Element-wise multiplication and powers apply to every stored time.
